about:
Moving from a different country, traveling around the world and interacting with diverse cultures during my career have helped me understand even deeper how important the hospitality industry is and how globally interconnected the world have become. From my first job out of college, I knew I was passionate about this industry.

Globally speaking, I truly enjoy learning and interacting with different regions around the world. One evening I could be negotiating a contract with a partner in Australia and next morning educating myself on a new acquired account in France and in the afternoon doing a strategy meeting in español with a client based in Colombia. 

I analyze data and reports to make knowledgeable recommendations to grow revenue streams as well as  partnership with clients and hotels. Very passionate about establishing, maintaining and advancing alliances with executives, buyers, travel agencies partners and hotels across the globe. 

Away from work, I am devoted to spend quality time with my family. We love traveling together, enjoy meeting friends near and far. I enjoy cooking, especially outdoors while camping. You can also find me in Yoga practice and Zumba classes, as dancing is another of my passions.

headline: Partner at Deloitte | Business Transformation Leader | Human Capital | Consumer Industry | 20+ years driving complex business transformation with a focus on strategic change, workforce strategy and employee experience
topSkills: Change Management • Organizational Design • Talent Strategy • Business Process Improvement • Business Transformation
about:
Over the last 19+ years, I have had the privilege of helping Retail and Consumer Products companies drive and realize complex business transformation through a comprehensive lens on workforce enablement, adoption and employee experience.

As a Principal (Partner) in Deloitte's Human Capital practice, I lead the Change Strategy & Analytics capability within Change Services and serve as a chief innovator of Deloitte's Change Services, Transformation Intelligence proprietary IP.  I advise global clients on transformation strategy and specialize in leading data-driven change management, reimagining operating model and organization design, evolving talent strategy and governance models, enabling leadership alignment, culture shift and enhanced workforce capabilities to drive business adoption with a focus on improving employee experience. 

I've seen how business adoption and improved employee experience make all the difference between "implementation" and true transformation, delivering value for shareholders, employees and customers.  

The programs I lead span multiple geographies, and range from enterprise wide to functional transformations including those in Finance, IT, HR, Supply Chain, Operations, and Commercial.  I have deep experience helping clients design and adopt standardized and industry-leading global business processes across functions, and I have led and delivered several technology-enabled transformations (SAP, Workday, Oracle, Coupa, Anaplan, etc.) including numerous multiyear, global SAP and Oracle and transformations, each of which delivered significant efficiencies and growth opportunities.

I lead high performing teams and I'm committed to the development of diverse talent, with a focus on inclusivity, responsibility and well-being.  

I hold a Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, and an MBA from Northwestern University (Kellogg). I'm currently living my best life in the Chicago area with my husband and our three children who keep us entertained and busy with basketball, football and gymnastics galore!

publications.title: Simplified Computational Modeling Approach for Analysis and Optimization of Temperbead Welding Procedures
publications.description:
Post weld heat treatment (PWHT) is a conventional approach in controlling hardness and toughness in the heat affected zone (HAZ) of weld overlays. However, in some applications PWHT can be impractical and/or can lead to loss of mechanical properties and embrittlement. Dissimilar Metal welds (DMWs) with low-alloy steels and austenitic nickel fillers made by machine GTAW & GMAW are common in the oil and gas industry, and usually require a PWHT. Some companies employ a temberbead welding (TBW) technique in lieu of a PWHT. TBW tempers the martensite formed in the HAZ of the steel by using the heat input from subsequent welds and weld layers. Current methodology for the development of TBW procedures are based heavily on trial and error which requires a lot of material and time, therefore, it is often not practical. A simplified and cost effective approach for the development of TBW procedures was the focus of this research. 
The approach used relies on JMatPro for prediction of thermo-physical properties of the utilized base metals and welding filler metals, while using ESI’s Visual-Environment / SYSWELD for finite element modeling (FEA) to accurately generate HAZ thermal histories. An approach for quantification of thermal histories was developed and applied to evaluate the efficiency of welding procedures in tempering the martensite that forms in the HAZ. The sequence of weld thermal cycles experienced in HAZ, their maximum temperatures, and the number of reheats within a predefined tempering temperature range were used as criteria for tempering efficiency evaluation.
The proposed methodology provides tools for layer-by-layer analysis of the tempering effect of each layer in DWOLs.

According to published data, the US healthcare system does not adequately or effectively transition pediatric cystic fibrosis patients to adult care. publications.title: More than Three Dozen IRS Letter Rulings Allow Late QOF Self-Certifications
publications.description: This article summarizes more than three dozen rulings issued by the IRS that permit taxpayers to make late self-certification elections for their Qualified Opportunity Funds (QOFs), which are tax-advantaged vehicles organized for the purpose of investing in certain low-income communities designated for economic development tax stimulus by the chief executives of every U.S. state and possession and the District of Columbia.

publications.title: Decertification of Qualified Opportunity Funds
publications.description: This article discusses how a self-certified Qualified Opportunity Fund (“QOF”) may relinquish that status through the QOF’s voluntary self-decertification or an involuntary decertification under the anti-abuse rules, and the consequences to tax-deferred investors in a QOF of either such decertification. It also discusses the recent guidance on QOF self-decertification, which initially appeared as a simple check-the-box election on line 6 of the November 6, 2020 draft of IRS Form 8996, Qualified Opportunity Fund, only to have that line removed entirely from the final version of that form. It also explores how the failure of the Internal Revenue Service to promulgate forms, instructions, or other guidance regarding the QOF’s voluntary self-decertification election necessitated change to the final regulation in “correcting amendments” issued on August 5, 2021, and how the current uncertainty surrounding the voluntary decertification process has impacted qualified opportunity zone funds and businesses that, due to the economic changes wrought by COVID-19, have lost their raison d’etre.

publications.title: COVID-19 Relief for Opportunity Zone Funds and Investors
publications.description: This Article describes how temporary changes to the qualified opportunity zone (QOZ) tax incentive, combined with new reliance regulations that clarify the requirements for qualified opportunity zone businesses (QOZBs) to modify their written plans to expend working capital in response to the ongoing coronavirus emergency, will make more individuals and entities eligible for federal tax stimulus by increasing flexibility for the qualified opportunity funds (QOFs) and QOZBs in which they invest to redeploy their capital into qualifying business development projects in a QOZ.

publications.title: On the Use and Abuse of Legislative History in the "Preparer Fraud" Doctrine
publications.description: For more than a century, U.S. tax evaders have been liable for unpaid tax at any time so that statutes of limitation do not stymie collection of fruits of fraud. Today, however, federal courts of appeal are split over a novel doctrine that holds unwitting victims of abusive tax professionals strictly and perpetually liable for their mistake. For eight years, the U.S. Tax Court followed by the Second Circuit Court of Appeals have promulgated a new rule of tax assessment masquerading under an historical veneer that for the first time eliminates repose from honest taxpayers who filed their returns in good faith. The Federal Circuit's recent decision to fight the doctrine of preparer fraud on first principles requires an accurate historical record for the Supreme Court to decide the contest, which this article finally provides.

publications.title: Major U.S. Tax Debt/Equity Rules Finalized
publications.description: A summary of new U.S. tax rules that recharacterize certain related-party debt instruments as equity and their implications for cross-border financing. publications.title: What Will Become of the U.S. Debt/Equity Proposal?
publications.description: Identifying key problems with U.S. Treasury's proposed regulations under section 385 of the Internal Revenue Code, later corrected in the October 2016 final regulations, that would have recharacterized short-term debt, cash-pooling arrangements and debt of highly-regulated financial companies as equity if issued within 6 years of certain distributions and reorganizations. See "Major U.S. tax debt/equity rules finalized" (available at: https://www.osler.com/en/resources/cross-border/2016/major-u-s-tax-debt-equity-rules-finalized).

publications.title: Preparing for Preparer Fraud - A Practitioner's Guide
publications.description:
That fraud vitiates all transactions is no less true of tax than of contract law. Congress’s first revenue law passed after ratification of the 16th Amendment extended by three years Treasury’s period for collecting taxes from fraudulent filers. Since 1919 that extension has been indefinite. 

This Tax Notes Special Report explores a curious line of cases arising out of the U.S. Tax Court's decision in Allen v. Commissioner (2007) which have all but eliminated the element of scienter in statute-of-limitation cases where a taxpayer's return is filed fraudulently, without the taxpayer's knowledge or consent. That doctrine was recently rejected by the Federal Court of Claims, in a decision upheld by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit and has been hotly litigated since this article appeared.

publications.title: The Paradox of Preparer Fraud
publications.description: Adam S. Wallwork provides a novel look at the United States Tax Court’s doctrine of preparer fraud, which recently provoked a circuit split. He shows that the Tax Court's preparer fraud doctrine is inconsistent with the language, history and policy of Code Sec. 6501(c)(1)’s fraudulent return exception and presents empirical evidence that the Tax Court's rule of strict liability for fraudulent returns (in the statute-of-limitations, though not the penalty context) actually increases fraud in the name of preventing it.

publications.title: What You Don't Know Can Hurt You: Paying for Preparer Fraud
publications.description: In this article, Adam Wallwork examines the circuit split that has recently developed over whether a return preparer's fraud is sufficient to toll the three-year statute of limitations on federal tax assessments indefinitely. By rejecting the United States Tax Court's rule, upheld by the Second Circuit Court of Appeals, the U.S. Court of Federal Claims and the Federal Circuit Court of Appeals have created a situation in which wealthy, well-advised taxpayers may be able to completely escape the perpetual liability and compound interest that their less-fortunate counterparts must face in tax deficiency litigation before the U.S. Tax Court. The article explores the policy implications of this continued disagreement between the federal government's primary venues for refund and deficiency actions.

headline: Managing Director - Supply Chain and Operations Consulting at Deloitte Consulting
about:
I am a Managing Director based in Milwaukee WI -- the heartland of US manufacturing, focused on supply chain, operations and technology.  The question I am most interested in is "how do we deploy technology, accounting for human need, in pursuit of value."  As a former college professor and teacher of supply chain and operations theory, I can get pretty passionate about "why it should be so...."  That is, how do the laws of economics and physics inform us about what to expect in the "real world."  Not an ivory tower guy, but someone who believes in a set of science-based principles.

Prior to joining Deloitte, I was an Associate Professor of Management at Marquette University and a Visiting Associate Professor of Operations Management at the University of Chicago, Booth School of Business. I have twice been the recipient of Marquette University’s Executive MBA program “Educator of the Year” award, and in 2012, I was the recipient of the John P. Raynor Award for Teaching Excellence. I also was a postdoctoral research fellow at Harvard Business School. Prior to my stint in academia, I held roles at both Ernst & Young and Andersen Consulting (now Accenture).

experience.position: Managing Director - Supply Chain and Operations Consulti
experience.description: Covering the waterfront for supply chain, operations, and technology - Author, Educator, Consultant.

I am the Research Director and leader of Deloitte’s Center for Integrated Research.  Along with my team, I collaboratively work with practitioners, clients, and other thought leaders to coordinate global, cross-sector, research for Deloitte.  The ultimate goal of my efforts is to develop proprietary insights that can be used to drive success for our clients and the firm. I routinely presents to global forums and work with practitioner and client teams in areas such as Industry 4.0, Internet of Things, Additive and Advanced Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Behavioral Economics and Management.  I am based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where I live with my wonderful wife and children.

Taught and conducted research on technology and supply chain management and co-led the Marquette University Center for Supply Chain Management. 

Named “Educator of the Year” in 2007 and 2009 and received the John P. Raynor Award for Teaching Excellence in 2012.

publications.title: Does scarcity make you dumb? A behavioral understanding of how scarcity diminishes our decision making and control
publications.description: When people lack the tools and resources needed to operate effectively, they fall prey to the scarcity mind-set. If left unchecked, scarcity can have deleterious effects on performance. The good news is, leaders have an opportunity to help prevent scarcity before it happens.

publications.title: 3D opportunity and the digital thread: Additive manufacturing ties it all together
publications.description: While additive manufacturing has become a crucial part of the design process, it has not reached critical mass at the enterprise level. The digital thread—a single, seamless strand of data that stretches from the initial design to the finished part—can help scale and enhance AM capabilities.

publications.title: Industry 4.0 and manufacturing ecosystems: Exploring the world of connected enterprises
publications.description: The marriage of advanced manufacturing techniques with information technology, data, and analytics is driving another industrial revolution—one that invites manufacturing leaders to combine information technology and operations technology to create value in new and different ways.

publications.title: Editorial: Behavioral insights- Putting Humans in the loop: Deloitte Review Issue 18
publications.description: As the march of “smart” technologies seemingly takes on a life of its own, it is worth remembering that advances in the behavioral sciences can better enable the human-centric design of programs, technologies, and organizations.

publications.title: Behavioral strategy to combat choice overload: A framework for managers
publications.description: Behavioral researchers have identified a dizzying array of concepts involved in applying “nudge” tactics to business management. Here’s a straightforward way for managers to make sense of them all.

publications.title: Inside the Internet of Things (IoT): A primer on the technologies building the IoT
publications.description: Explore the inner workings of the Internet of Things in this deep dive into some of the technologies that make it possible.

publications.title: Ignoring bad news: How behavioral factors influence us to sugarcoat or avoid negative messages
publications.description: People will often ignore or even distort the information they collect when it is “bad news.” How does this impact organizational learning and performance—and what, if anything, can or should businesses do about it?

publications.title: The more things change: Value creation, value capture, and the Internet of Things
publications.description: Some changes enabled by the Internet of Things will be incremental, while others will be transformative. Yet the need to capture value remains as acute as ever. The established principles of strategic differentiation, process flow, and network economics will go a long way toward revealing a path to long-term success.

publications.title: Editorial: Master or servant? Deloitte Review Issue 17
publications.description: Making the most of IoT-enabled capabilities, while avoiding the temptations of change for its own sake, requires understanding what is likely to change, and what isn’t. Organizations must still think carefully about value capture, for which proven constructs such as competitive position and competitive advantage remain indispensable.

publications.title: 3D opportunity for the future: Industry participants speak out: Deloitte Review Issue 17
publications.description: Additive manufacturing continues to expand and, as the technologies move beyond prototyping, managers struggle with how to apply AM within their businesses. Data from our 3D Opportunity course suggest where stakeholders want to see AM investments made, and how to assess the benefits these avenues of choice provide.

publications.title: Going rogue: How behavioral factors affect decisions related to work process deviation
publications.description: Deviation from standard work processes is common. But rather than view process deviation as the enemy, companies can use it to drive positive outcomes by applying behavioral principles in the workplace.

publications.title: Stop or not? How behavioral factors affect decisions related to work interruptions
publications.description: What can managers do to combat productivity losses caused by distractions and interruptions? In some cases, common-sense interventions carry the day. But in others, a counterintuitive approach turns out to be more effective.

publications.title: 3D opportunity for end-use products: Additive manufacturing builds a better future
publications.description: As the technology improves, product manufacturers are increasingly using additive manufacturing (AM) to enable new designs and improve product performance relative to products manufactured with conventional techniques.

publications.title: 3D opportunity for production: Additive manufacturing makes its (business) case: Deloitte Review Issue 15
publications.description: The business case for additive manufacturing (AM) starts with careful consideration of the direct costs driving AM and traditional production economics, and continues with an examination of less direct factors that can add dramatic value for companies and their customers.

publications.title: 3D opportunity in aerospace and defense: Additive manufacturing takes flight
publications.description: The aerospace and defense industry is increasingly using additive manufacturing to reduce material costs, decrease labor content, and increase availability of parts at point of use, which may have a dramatic impact on the supply chain.

publications.title: 3D opportunity in medical technology: Additive manufacturing comes to life
publications.description: Additive manufacturing capabilities align well with the needs of the medical device segment, enhancing product customization and enabling efficient, cost-effective production and delivery.

publications.title: 3D opportunity in tooling: Additive manufacturing shapes the future
publications.description: The use of additive manufacturing to fabricate tooling can not only reduce lead times and costs, but also improve functionality and enhance the ability to customize.

publications.title: The 3D opportunity primer:  The basics of additive manufacturing
publications.description: If the past is prologue, the role that additive manufacturing (3D printing) plays in the manufacturing value chain will likely grow in scope, scale, and complexity.  This article provides an overview of additive manufacturing for those who are new to this important emerging process.

publications.title: 3D printing: "Complexity is free"​ may be costly for some
publications.description: Additive manufacturing (AM)—the proper technical term for 3D printing—is likely to have an enormous impact on all our lives, but that doesn’t mean it’s going to be good for every business.

publications.title: It's called research: The Exceptional Company collection
publications.description: The path to discovery is seldom straight. Rarely does the reader of the final research have the opportunity to understand how the journey of discovery unfolded.

publications.title: 3D Opportunity: Additive manufacturing paths to performance, innovation, and growth
publications.description: Additive manufacturing technology can break existing performance trade-offs by reducing the capital needed to achieve scale and scope economies. Understanding how this can be done requires a review of how scale and scope economies shape certain product manufacturing and distribution decisions.

publications.title: The answer is 9,142: Understanding the influence of disruption risk on inventory decision making
publications.description: The question was how many units of inventory a manager should order when faced with a possible disruption in supply. The correct answer is not guesswork, but based on 150 years of theory and practice. We examine individual choices made in this critical situation—and the results are not encouraging.

publications.title: Location, location, location
publications.description: Sometimes, it makes sense to spend more to conveniently locate capacity.

publications.title: Location, learning, and logistics: A framework for managing trade-offs in capacity location decisions
publications.description: Business leaders who misjudge the location of production relative to the location of product and process development resources may adversely impact the company’s long-term competitive position. We explore the link between production location decisions, the nature of the capabilities required to create a product, and the ability of a company to develop the next-generation technologies it may seek.

Exceptional companies face a trade-off between increasing ROA through return on sales (ROS) or through total asset turnover (TAT), and the best performers systematically choose higher ROS. We now focus on the primary driver of superior profitability, ROS, and on its determinants: revenue and cost.

Last fall, the University of Chicago's Harris School of Public Policy and Mansueto Institute for Urban Innovation launched the second Harris Policy Innovation Challenge seeking bold, actionable solutions to the question: What can Chicago do over the next three years to create a thriving Loop for the next 20 years?

One team's proposal aims to extend the 606 elevated park trail through downtown to Ping Tom Memorial Park, implement co-living floors in buildings undergoing commercial-to-residential transition and develop urban vertical agriculture to address the Loop's chronic fresh-food desert.

I hold an IFRS Foundation’s Fundamentals of Sustainability Accounting (FSA) credential and am a CPA in the state of Wisconsin.

When I am out of the office, I enjoy spending time with outdoors, with family, keeping up my French language skills and playing piano.

receivedRecommendations.description:
You couldn't force me to share a valid complaint about Elisabeth Sullivan as a leader or editor. I mean, you could try, but I'd be lying if I said anything. 
 
Elisabeth is the manager I will always compare other managers to. She's a gifted leader who engendered trust and admiration on our team. She was able to quickly and effectively inspire us to change and improve. She's an enthusiastic mentor who is always available to help her team grow. She's intelligent and insightful, transparent, patient, strategic, never reactionary. She's also authentic, cool, unflappable and affable, as well as comfortable and at-ease with anyone at any level. She is the manager who no one ever complained about when she wasn't around. 

And she happens to be a superb journalist and editor, too! I will always be a much better writer and editor because of my time working with her. As an editor, she’s a true partner. She inspired me to do my best writing, and then helped me take it to another level.  

She founded a prolific and universally admired editorial function within our firm that I am so proud to be a part of. She built a stellar team, helped us forge strong ties with each other and to company leaders. She took a nearly a non-existent function that many doubted could work in a firm like ours and transformed it into an indispensable team of in-demand and highly respected writers and editors. It seems understated to say she left our thought leadership function in a better place. She brought it into being. She made it really good. She left us on a rapidly ascending trajectory that she set in motion, all while giving her team credit for our successes. To say she is missed also feels like an understatement.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Changing the World One Woman at a Time
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: November 18, 2019, Anne worked with Elisabeth but on different teams
receivedRecommendations.description:
Elisabeth truly is a big picture thinker.  She is not stuck on one track.  We have collaborated to run expert think tank sessions where we gather disparate ZS experts to talk about the future of the healthcare and/or pharma industries.  This group of ZS partners has very strong opinions, which can make it difficult to extract a cohesive point of view.  Elisabeth weaves the story threads together, considering all components at all times to come to a powerful, provocative story line.  She also always has the end audience in mind which shapes the way she pitches the story line.

One of the values that my business school espouses is “confidence without attitude.”  This is something that Elisabeth exhibits in spades.  In meetings she speaks with authority and even when she is disagreeing with the direction that the conversation is going or asserting a different view, there is no attitude about it.  She doesn’t make the other people feel wrong or foolish about their views.  Instead she speaks, we listen and adapt the direction of the story because what she says makes sense!  And we all leave the meeting feeling better than when we entered and confident that we just experienced a moment of synergy – where Elisabeth’s contributions really made the outcome more than the sum of the parts.  

During the think tank sessions, she is often quite reserved.  She thinks about what to say / interject and then waits to see if the experts get to those points on their own.  If so, she allows for the free flow of ideas and the conversation to continue uninterrupted.  If there are important ideas which they don’t bring up, she gracefully finds a way to add them in.  And at the end of the session, she often can bring the points together in a way where people can clearly see what the next steps are in developing the opinion piece.   
 
She is someone who embodies courageous curiosity.  She is willing to jump into the process to play around with ideas out loud to see where they will head and how we can build on each other’s knowledge and insight.  Her previous experience as an editor makes her an invaluable thought partner.  I can relax and free range with my ideas / connections and know that she is holding the container to make the pieces make sense and to distill the most compelling parts of the ideas – the “so what.”  Elisabeth’s strong grounding in the industry and how she tracks the news makes her able to discern which ideas / story lines are older or stale and which ones really haven’t been covered yet in the media.  This helps us throw away some of the story lines – not because they aren’t interesting but because we have limited resources and need to apply them where it matters most.  

Elisabeth is a delight to work with and is always looking to innovate the process through which we gather and distill ideas. With her, there is no sacred process that we need to continue to follow. Instead she is always on the alert for ways to make the process work better.

publications.title: Facebook Messenger: Eroding User Privacy in Order to Collect, Analyze, and Sell Your Personal Information.
publications.publishedAt: The John Marshall Journal of Information Technology and Privacy Law
publications.description:
http://repository.jmls.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1767&context=jitpl

This comment examines Facebook‘s new standalone Facebook Messenger app, and reviews how the Privacy Policy, Data Use Policy, and the list of permissions violate Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act. The comment focuses on Facebook Messenger‘s deceptive methods of accessing users‘ personal information and how Facebook uses that personal information. Section II explains social networking sites and the configuration of Facebook, Facebook Messenger, and Facebook‘ s evolving policies. Section II also discusses the Federal Trade Commission and the Federal Trade Commission Act that was created to protect consumers against unfair, deceptive, or fraudulent practices. Section III will identify Facebook‘s prior commitments and obligations it had to users and demonstrate how the site failed to protect users in the past. The comment then addresses latent issues that arise out of Facebook Messenger‘s list of permissions, policies, and how it violates Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act. Finally, the Comment presents a consumer-based proposal outlining the necessary changes to avoid violating Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act. The proposal addresses privacy and data use concerns while continuing to uphold the Federal Trade Commission Act in Facebook‘s day-to-day activity.

about:
Brandon is a ServiceNow Certified System Administrator with specialized expertise in Customer Service Management (CSM) and Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) implementations. Known for his meticulous attention to detail, Brandon excels in designing and developing end-to-end web applications and guiding complex ServiceNow projects from concept to deployment. His deep understanding of IT Service Management (ITSM), CSM, and the transformative capabilities of the ServiceNow platform positions him as a strategic asset in enterprise digital transformation initiatives.

At Deloitte, Brandon played a pivotal role in delivering high-impact ServiceNow solutions across a range of modules, including CSM, GRC, Field Service Management, Service Portal, and the Now Experience Framework. His ability to integrate these tools enabled him to streamline operations, automate workflows, and enhance organizational performance. He also engineered custom integrations and bespoke solutions tailored to client-specific needs—especially in regulated industries—ensuring compliance, scalability, and measurable impact.

Prior to Deloitte, Brandon expanded his ServiceNow expertise with a strong focus on Application Portfolio Management, Demand Intake, and the development of custom workflow approvals designed to meet rigorous auditing and compliance standards. He was also responsible for creating detailed technical documentation, conducting end-user training, and driving change management to support successful platform adoption.

Brandon’s web development and data visualization skills complement his ServiceNow capabilities. He has developed robust applications using Java Spring Boot, .NET, and designed data-driven dashboards in Splunk. His solutions provided stakeholders with actionable insights through intuitive and responsive visualizations, highlighting his proficiency in both back-end development and user experience design.

With a strong foundation in web technologies, platform architecture, and technical recruiting, Brandon brings a holistic and solutions-oriented mindset to every engagement. His unique combination of technical depth and business alignment makes him an ideal fit for organizations seeking a forward-thinking developer who can drive innovation through custom ServiceNow integrations, GRC excellence, and cross-functional collaboration.

projects.title: Photonic Crystal De-multiplexer: Analysis and Simulation
projects.description: Super-prism, which is a new phenomenon in photonic crystal, has recently attracted much attention. The phenomenon is due to the anomalous dispersion of frequencies out of the photonic crystal band gap. The group velocity dispersion in photonic crystal for wavelengths lower than the photonic band gap (known as the S-vector super-prism phenomenon) has found its main application in de-multiplexing. However, due to the excessive band curvature which is coincident with high dispersion, the overall S-vector super-prism resolution is what was originally hoped. In this research, the numerical methods for analysis and simulation of demultiplexers are reviewed and the propagation of light wave in two photonic crystals with different lattice has been simulated. The effect of variation of radii and refractive indices has been studied in these two structures. Finally, the propagation of oblique light has been investigated

about:
I help banks and financial institutions navigate regulatory pressure, rising alert volumes, and cost constraints by building scalable, technology-enabled AML and financial crime compliance programs. I work at the intersection of regulation, operations, and execution, helping institutions strengthen risk management while improving efficiency and delivery outcomes.

Over the last 16+ years, I have led AML, sanctions, and fraud risk initiatives across advisory, managed services, and regulatory remediation engagements. My experience spans building and scaling teams, leading multi-country delivery, and advising senior stakeholders across India, APAC, Europe, and the Middle East.

I am best known for building and scaling financial crime operations at enterprise scale, setting up global delivery and managed services models, and helping institutions respond to regulatory scrutiny with speed, structure, and confidence. Much of my work involves complex operating environments where volumes are high, timelines are tight, and regulatory expectations continue to evolve.

My approach is pragmatic and execution-focused. I place strong emphasis on operating models, governance, delivery discipline, and data-driven decision-making, alongside frameworks and policy. I believe effective compliance functions are built through clear accountability, resilient processes, and teams that can perform under sustained regulatory and operational pressure.

Currently, my focus is on scaling financial crime managed services, driving technology-enabled compliance transformation, and supporting institutions in preparation for regulatory reviews, supervisory examinations, and model validations across transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and customer risk assessment.

experience.description:
I lead large-scale financial crime compliance and forensic initiatives for banks, NBFCs, and financial institutions, helping them strengthen AML, sanctions, and fraud risk management while improving operational efficiency and regulatory outcomes.

My role spans strategy, delivery, and scale, with a focus on building sustainable, technology-enabled compliance capabilities across geographies.

I have built and scaled a Financial Crime Compliance team from approximately 40 to over 275 professionals, supporting advisory, managed services, and regulatory remediation engagements. slides.title: How to be The Perfect Corporate Yes-Man: A Masterclass in Climbing the Ladder Without Breaking a Sweat
slides.subtitle: Manish Mandhyan on LinkedIn
slides.description: (First post in a series of posts where I explore the age old questions of "How to be...or not be!") Have you ever wondered how some people climb the corporate ladder with seemingly little effort, while others are left at the bottom rung, gasping for air? Well, I've got a secret for you—it's not about talent, intelligence, or even hard work. It's about mastering the subtle art of becoming the Perfect Corporate Yes-Man. Ready to transform your career? Let's dive in! Rule #1: Agree, then Ask What You're Agreeing To In the world of Yes-Men, it's 'agree first, think later.' Your boss wants to launch a new project on a Friday afternoon? Fantastic idea! (Then go home and figure out how you're going to cancel all your weekend plans.) Rule #2: Master the Nod and Smile Body language is your best friend. When in doubt, nod. When extremely in doubt, nod while smiling. This universal gesture says, 'I'm on board, even if I have no idea what I'm on board with.' Rule #3: Ambiguity is Your Ally Never commit to a firm yes or no when a vague answer will do. Phrases like 'I'll look into it,' or 'Let's circle back on this,' are your go-to responses. They're non-committal, yet give the illusion of action—a Yes-Man's dream! Rule #4: Be Everywhere, Yet Nowhere The key to being a successful Yes-Man is visibility. You want to be seen at every meeting, every event, every team lunch. But don't stand out; blend in. Your goal is to be as non-threatening as possible while agreeing with everyone in the room. Rule #5: Know When to Say No (Just Kidding!) A Yes-Man never says no. But if you absolutely must, disguise it as a yes. For example, 'Yes, I think that's something we can consider for the next quarter,' is a polite way of pushing the problem onto Future You. And let's face it, Future You is much better equipped to handle it. Congratulations! You're now well on your way to becoming the Perfect Corporate Yes-Man. Say goodbye to the stress and strain of independent thought and hello to a life of agreeable mediocrity. You won't regret it (because you won't have the option to). But Wait, Think Before You Yes! Cautionary Tale #1: The Sinking Ship While it's tempting to say 'yes' to please upper management, doing so without proper evaluation can lead you straight into the Titanic of projects. Just because the captain (read: your boss) thinks it's a good idea to speed ahead doesn't mean you should ignore the iceberg up front. Remember, the Yes-Man goes down with the ship, too. Cautionary Tale #2: The Echo Chamber Continuously agreeing with your boss or team without offering alternative viewpoints can create an echo chamber. This might make meetings end faster, but it also stifles innovation and problem-solving. When everyone in the room is a Yes-Man, you risk missing out on crucial insights that could be beneficial to the company. In this case, your 'yes' isn't just a disservice to you, but to the entire organization. Cautionary Tale #3: The Credibility Gap When you agree to everything, people may start to question your judgement. After all, not every idea can be a good one. The more you say 'yes,' the more you risk eroding your own credibility. When the time comes for you to genuinely advocate for something, your words might fall on skeptical ears. Cautionary Tale #4: The Burnout Agreeing to take on every task that comes your way may make you the go-to person in a crunch, but it also makes you the go-to person for burnout. Spreading yourself too thin can impact the quality of your work and your well-being. As the saying goes, 'If you try to catch two rabbits, you won't catch either.' Final Thoughts: The Paradox of the Yes-Man Ah, the life of a Yes-Man—it's not all sunshine, rainbows, and yearly bonuses. As we've seen, mindlessly nodding along can lead to some pretty disastrous outcomes. So, the next time you're tempted to say 'yes' without thinking, remember: Sometimes the most powerful word in business isn't 'yes,' it's 'why?' And if you ever find yourself in a room full of Yes-Men, be the one to break the cycle. After all, the corporate world could use a little more thought and a little less nodding. But hey, if you've read this far, you're either intrigued, or you're practicing your Yes-Man skills by agreeing with everything I've said. Either way, I'll take it as a win!

slides.title: How to be an Office Guru: A Satirical Guide to Becoming the Workplace Philosopher
slides.subtitle: Manish Mandhyan on LinkedIn
slides.description: In the vast ecosystem of the corporate world, the Office Guru stands out as the enigmatic figure, ever-ready to sprinkle wisdom over daily monotony. From turning team meetings into TED Talks to transforming email threads into philosophical debates, the Office Guru is a force to be reckoned with. Ready to ascend to this exalted position? Let's begin. Rule #1: Speak in Parables When asked for input, never provide a straightforward answer. Opt for parables or anecdotes that require at least two levels of interpretation. For example, when discussing quarterly goals, remind your team that 'Rome wasn't built in a day, but they were laying bricks every hour.' Rule #2: Quote the Unquotable Forget Steve Jobs or Warren Buffet; the Office Guru quotes figures like Socrates, Nietzsche, or even Yoda. The more unrelated to business, the better. It adds an air of intellectual complexity to even the most mundane office tasks. Rule #3: Maintain an Aura of Mystery The Office Guru never reveals too much. Whether it's your weekend plans or your thoughts on the new coffee machine, keep people guessing. A little mystery makes your wisdom seem all the more profound. Rule #4: Turn Everything Into a Life Lesson Missed a deadline? That's a lesson on the impermanence of time. Budget cuts? A hard look at the philosophy of scarcity. Turn every situation into a life lesson, and you'll have your colleagues looking to you for wisdom—or at least some comic relief. Rule #5: Your Desk is Your Temple An Office Guru's desk is not just a workspace; it's a sanctuary. Think Buddha statues, a Zen garden, and maybe a copy of 'The Art of War' conspicuously placed for all to see. Your desk should scream 'I'm enlightened,' even if your overflowing inbox suggests otherwise. Conclusion: So there you have it—the path to becoming the Office Guru you were always meant to be. As you embrace your new role, remember: The Guru doesn't seek followers; followers seek the Guru. Or something like that. Namaste, corporate warriors. But Wait, Think Before You Guru! Cautionary Tale #1: The Pseudo-Intellectual Trap While spouting philosophical quotes can make you sound wise, there's a fine line between being an Office Guru and a pseudo-intellectual. Make sure your wisdom actually adds value, or you might find your colleagues tuning you out faster than you can say 'existential crisis.' Cautionary Tale #2: The Overcomplication Turning everything into a life lesson can sometimes backfire, especially if you're obscuring simple facts with elaborate metaphors. Remember, not every situation requires a Socratic dialogue—sometimes a yes or no will do. Cautionary Tale #3: The Expectation Burden Being the Office Guru can lead to high expectations. Before you know it, you're the go-to person for every moral, ethical, or even technical dilemma in the office. Make sure you're prepared to handle the pressure, or your guru status might just turn into guru stress. Cautionary Tale #4: The Guru-Go-Round While it's fun to be the center of attention, remember that today's Guru could be tomorrow's forgotten sage. The corporate world is fickle, and new heroes (or gurus) are born every day. Don't get too attached to your newfound status. Final Thoughts: The Guru's Dilemma So there you have it, the highs and lows of becoming an Office Guru. While your newfound wisdom may bring you a cult following, beware the pitfalls that come with the role. After all, the wise man knows that he knows nothing—or was it the other way around? Either way, keep guru-ing responsibly.

publications.title: Sucesses and Shortcomings: Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration in Eastern and Central Africa
publications.description: In post-conflict transitions, disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration have played a crucial role in the treatment of former combatants and the advancement of peacebuilding. This peacebuilding process, known as DDR, has experienced successes and failures throughout its implementation across the globe. Specifically, as conflict erupted across many nations in Central and Eastern Africa, the disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration programs that were implemented during different nations’ peacebuilding transition towards at the turn of the twenty-first century experienced variations among their success at reducing or halting the conflict. This investigation analyzes the factors that contribute to the ability for disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration programs to successfully reduce conflict by examining the implementation of these systems in Rwanda, Burundi, and the Democratic Republic of Congo from 1997 to 2012. The factors analyzed in this study include the time it takes to implement disarmament, the number of parties that commit to the peace agreement, the robustness of reintegration and vocational training curriculum, and the amount of funding that each program receives. Throughout this comparative analysis, these factors demonstrate to influence the success of disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration programs, however, some of these variables are more influential to success than others.

publications.title: Unveiling Your Layers: A Journey to Authentic Self-Discovery
publications.description: Sergio Rodriguez shares his personal journey towards authentic self-discovery, emphasizing that authenticity is a continuous process. He discusses navigating stereotypes, confronting personal battles with mental health, and embracing his Latin roots and cultural identity. The article highlights the importance of embracing all facets of one's identity and encourages others to embark on their own journeys of self-discovery.

publications.title: Equity in Motion: LGBTQIA+ Considerations in Global Mobility
publications.description: When we first read Deloitte Global's 2023 LGBT+ Inclusion@Work report, we were struck by a startling statistic: one-third of LGBTQIA+ professionals globally are actively seeking more inclusive employers. This isn't just a number—it should be a wake-up call for employers worldwide. So, what does this mean for us in the ever-evolving landscape of the future of work? Let's unpack this together.

publications.title: Navigating the World, Navigating Inclusion: Sergio Rodriguez
publications.description: The article, 'Navigating the World, Navigating Inclusion: Sergio Rodriguez,' dives into my journey at Deloitte, blending personal stories with my passion for DEI. It covers everything from my beginnings as a young Latino gay man in the business world to my current work in global workforce inclusivity. It's a real look at how my experiences, including growing up in Costa Rica, have fueled my drive to create a workplace where everyone can be their true selves.

publications.title: Activating equity in the workplace through talent mobility
publications.description:
Leading practices for Global Talent Mobility

Too often, Global Talent Mobility and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) remain disconnected, potentially limiting an organization’s ability to retain and grow top talent on a global scale. By embracing this responsibility for DEI, Global Talent Mobility leaders can extend their influence and impact across the entire organization, align to a key C-suite priority, and push their organization towards its broader economic and social goals.

honorsAndAwards.description:
These global lists by INvolve - The Inclusion People champion trailblazers across businesses who are driving positive change for LGBTQ+ employees globally.

"As a Tax Senior Manager, Sergio helps organizations manage their cross-border employees, address worldwide tax obligations, and develop and retain a powerful global workforce. publications.title: Genetic deletion of miR-204 improves glycemic control despite obesity in db/db mice
publications.publishedAt: Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications · Oct 29, 2020
publications.description: Investigated whether the absence of miR-204 rescues the impaired glycemic control and obesity in the genetically diabetic (db/db) mice. We found that the db/db mice overexpressed miR-204 in the islets. The db/db mice lacking miR-204 (db/db-204-/-) initially develops hyperglycemia and obesity like the control (db/db) mice but later displayed a gradual improvement in glycemic control despite remaining obese. The db/db-204-/- mice had a lower fasting blood glucose and higher serum insulin level compared to the db/db mice. A homeostatic model assessment (HOMA) suggests the improvement of β-cell function contributes to the improvement in glycemic control in db/db-204-/- mice. Next, we examined the cellular proliferation and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and found an increased frequency of proliferating cells (PCNA + ve) and a decreased CHOP expression in the islets of db/db-204-/- mice. Next, we determined the effect of systemic miR-204 inhibition in improving glycemic control in the high-fat diet (HFD)-fed insulin-resistant mice. MiR-204 inhibition for 6 weeks improved the HFD-triggered impairment in glucose disposal. In conclusion, the absence of miR-204 improves β-cell proliferation, decreases islet ER stress, and improves glycemic control with limited change in body weight in obese mice.

publications.title: Adipose Triglyceride Lipase Is a Key Lipase for the Mobilization of Lipid Droplets in Human β-Cells and Critical for the Maintenance of Syntaxin 1a Levels in β-Cells
publications.description: We found that glucose increases lipolysis in nondiabetic human islets but not in islets in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), indicating dysregulation of lipolysis in T2D islets. Silencing adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) in human pseudoislets with shRNA targeting ATGL (shATGL) increased triglycerides (TGs) and the number and size of LDs, indicating that ATGL is the principal lipase in human β-cells. In shATGL pseudoislets, biphasic glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS), and insulin secretion to 3-isobutyl-1-methylxanthine and KCl were all reduced without altering oxygen consumption rate compared with scramble control. Like human islets, INS1 cells showed visible LDs, glucose-responsive lipolysis, and impairment of GSIS after ATGL silencing. ATGL-deficient INS1 cells and human pseudoislets showed reduced SNARE protein syntaxin 1a (STX1A), a key SNARE component. Proteasomal degradation of Stx1a was accelerated likely through reduced palmitoylation in ATGL-deficient INS1 cells. Therefore, ATGL is responsible for LD mobilization in human β-cells and supports insulin secretion by stabilizing STX1A. The dysregulated lipolysis may contribute to LD accumulation and β-cell dysfunction in T2D islets.

publications.title: Lentiviral Mediated Gene Silencing in Human Pseudoislet Prepared in Low Attachment Plates
publications.description: We developed a detailed protocol for the creation of human pseudoislets after lentiviral transduction using two commercially available multiwell plates is described. The protocol can be easily performed and allows for efficient downregulation of genes and assessment of dynamism of insulin secretion using human islet cells. Thus, human pseudoislets with lentiviral mediated gene modulation provide a powerful and versatile model to assess gene function within human islet cells.

publications.title: Connecting pancreatic islet lipid metabolism with insulin secretion and the development of type 2 diabetes
publications.publishedAt: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences · Apr 2, 2019
publications.description: Obesity is the major contributing factor for the increased prevalence of type 2 diabetes (T2D) in recent years. Sustained positive influx of lipids is considered to be a precipitating factor for beta cell dysfunction and serves as a connection between obesity and T2D. Importantly, fatty acids (FA), a key building block of lipids, are a double-edged sword for beta cells. FA acutely increase glucose-stimulated insulin secretion through cell-surface receptor and intracellular pathways. However, chronic exposure to FA, combined with elevated glucose, impair the viability and function of beta cells in vitro and in animal models of obesity (glucolipotoxicity), providing an experimental basis for the propensity of beta cell demise under obesity in humans. To better understand the two-sided relationship between lipids and beta cells, we present a current view of acute and chronic handling of lipids by beta cells and implications for beta cell function and health. We also discuss an emerging role for lipid droplets (LD) in the dynamic regulation of lipid metabolism in beta cells and insulin secretion, along with a potential role for LD under nutritional stress in beta cells, and incorporate recent advancement in the field of lipid droplet biology.

publications.title: Delivery of shRNA via lentivirus in human pseudoislets provides a model to test dynamic regulation of insulin secretion and gene function in human islets
publications.description: We tested whether pseudoislets, created by dissociation and reaggregation of islet cell suspensions, allow for assessment of dynamic islet function after genetic modulation. Characterization of pseudoislets cultured for 1 week revealed better preservation of first-phase glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) compared with cultured-intact islets and insulin secretion profiles similar to fresh islets when challenged by glibenclamide and KCl. qPCR indicated that pseudoislets are similar to the original islets for the expression of markers for cell types, beta cell function, and cellular stress with the exception of reduced proinflammatory cytokine genes (IL1B, CCL2, CXCL8). The expression of extracellular matrix markers (ASPN, COL1A1, COL4A1) was also altered in pseudoislets compared with intact islets. Compared with intact islets transduced by adenovirus, pseudoislets transduced by lentivirus showed uniform transduction and better first-phase GSIS. Lastly, the lentiviral-mediated delivery of short hairpin RNA targeting glucokinase (GCK) achieved significant reduction of GCK expression in pseudoislets as well as marked reduction of both first and second phase GSIS without affecting the insulin secretion in response to KCl. Thus, pseudoislets are a tool that enables efficient genetic modulation of human islet cells while preserving insulin secretion.

headline: Applied Artificial Intelligence Consultant @Deloitte
about:
I come from a family which have had history of having commerce as majors, thus the institutional love for mathematics comes inherently. But there was also other part of growing up where I used to invest most of my time gaming on my PC specifically NFS, Age of Empires, etc. I always had a deep desire for knowing how these games are made or how to make my own program which works on click of a button. As the time progressed, I kept on developing my knowledge in Math from basic fractions leading to integrations and in programming starting from language as LOGO, BASIC then moving to Python, JAVA, COBOL. 

This passion carried me to get a job at TCS where I learned about new fields which would totally connect with me. Here the coding part would be the front face for my analysis of real-world problem whose solution would be achieved through mathematical approach.  But to learn and amplify my knowledge I pursued my masters at UIC. Here there were more resources available to me than I could have ever imagined as a kid. I learnt new languages, algorithm, compilers, higher mathematics, all with the same enthusiasm that drove me since my childhood. 

Currently I am working at Deloitte in the Applied Artificial Intelligence domain where the zeal to grow keeps getting better and is leading to me where it always led learn more and more.

Tools and programming languages: Python, GCP, AWS, EC2, SQL, MySQL, PySpark, JAVA, R, SAS, Power BI, MS Excel, MS Word, MS PowerPoint.

headline: Principal at Deloitte
about:
I am a Principal/Partner in Deloitte's Customer Strategy Consulting practice where I work with companies to drive customer and employee service transformation projects (from strategy to technology to managed services).  I serve clients within the financial services industry, and I previously led projects in the hospitality and retail industries.  I began my career as an Analyst at Deloitte in 2007.

In addition to client service, I serve as the National Leader of Deloitte's Analyst (pre-graduate school) community, including driving Analysts' experience and their learning and development.  This includes 4000 junior professionals within Deloitte's Strategy, Technology, and Human Capital practices, across both our private and public sector work.  Previously, I served as the National Deputy Leader of this program, as well as led the US Consulting practice's global pro bono work for our Analyst community.  In this role, I led on-the-ground pro bono engagements in Bolivia, Ghana, Northern Ireland, and Italy.

Outside of Deloitte, I serve on boards at the Ravinia Festival (an internationally renowned, 15,000-capacity, not-for-profit music venue) and Chicago's Shedd Aquarium (soon celebrating 100 years of sparking compassion, curiosity, and conservation for the aquatic animal world).

headline: Human Capital Clients & Markets Leader, Principal, Deloitte Consulting
about:
Nicole Patterson, a Principal with Deloitte's Workforce Transformation consulting practice, has over two decades of experience in global talent transformation, organizational transformation, global mobility, diversity equity and inclusion and change-management. She has consulted across industries, with an emphasis in the technology, media and entertainment sectors. She has led work at some of Silicon Valley's marquee companies.

Nicole is recognized by her clients and teams as an innovative, inspiring leader and problem-solver. She has scaled up and led inter-disciplinary, globally-dispersed, large teams. She has strong global experience, having also lived and worked abroad.

Early in her career, Nicole co-founded and was president of a leadership development company, CUBIS Group, which focused on experiential education for mid-level professionals. 

Nicole holds a Masters of Business Administration (MBA) with honors from University of Chicago’s Booth School of Business. She received her Bachelor of Arts in Political Science with honors from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA).  She is also a certified Global Professional in Human Resources (GPHR).

Nicole is a Board Member of Girls Inc. of Alameda County, an organization whose mission is to inspire all girls to be strong, smart and bold. 

Nicole is married and has two young children.

headline: Government and Public Services Senior Consultant
about: I believe in using human-centered design techniques to develop data-driven solutions that make the world a more efficient, equitable and ethical place. I’ve leveraged my coaching and management skills to help teach 5 courses and lead a team of 24 editors and writers to publish over 40 articles for CPR. My quantitative training as a macroeconomist and my writing skills as a Harris Writing Fellow have made me a powerful communicator who uses robust research and concisely written work to develop compelling policy solutions.

experience.companyName: Harris School of Public Policy at the University of Chicago
experience.description: As a writing fellow I coach Harris students on their writing projects, anything from cover letters to resumes, to opinion pieces or policy memos. I love to help writers find the best way to impact their reader through robust research and concise and compelling language.

I've been a teaching assistant for the following graduate courses: Analytical Politics 1 and Analytical Politics 2, the undergraduate courses: Policy Implementation and Policy Practicum, and the credential course: Persuasive Writing. As a TA I strive to collaborate directly with students, from brainstorming ideas for research, completing difficult math-based models, or revising and finalizing writing pieces.

As head of the editorial board, my role is to coordinate with senior editors and staff writers and shape the editorial direction of online publications by selecting topics and ensuring written content is concise, compelling, and well written.

As a summer 2021 Research Assistant intern at the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars, I worked with Scholar Ambassador Earl Anthony Wayne at the Mexico Institute. In this role I conducted background research; clarified research topics, attended congressional hearings, and updated presentations. I also interviewed experts in order to publish an article about the impact of USMCA on agriculture. Lastly, I guided event development by clarifying topic concepts, creating invitee lists, writing background briefs, and organizing post-meeting notes.

As an intern with the Chicago Justice Project, I collected, cleaned, and analyzed data about violence against women from several large databases, including the Chicago Police Department, the State’s Attorney Office and the Office of Emergency Management. I then developed this data analysis into an article about the difficulty in studying violence against women and the need for better data collection on violence against women in Chicago

I was promoted from Economist II to Senior Economist after taking responsibility for forecasting of higher-profile countries and increasing client interaction. I am primarily in charge of forecasting for Chile, Colombia, and Bolivia, as well as several smaller countries including Paraguay, Guyana, and Costa Rica.

I work on the Economics and Country risk team, focusing on Latin America and the Caribbean. I analyze, translate, and summarize important fiscal, public, and monetary policy developments and construct, maintain and update macroeconomic and sovereign risk forecasting models for Latin American and Caribbean countries. As an analyst I also respond to client questions by providing unique economic analysis in English and Spanish. Finally, I collaborate with political and energy analysts to write in-depth special reports on newsworthy topics about political, fiscal or economic updates.

volunteering.description: As a Harris Community Action fellow I am teamed up with the Chicago non-profit Equiticity, which advocates for racial equity through policy changes in the transportation landscape. I work one-on-one and in groups conducting lessons in math, writing, reading, science and history. headline: Managing Director at Deloitte Tax LLP
about:
Christine is a Managing Director in the Global Employer Services practice of the Chicago office of Deloitte Tax LLP, with over 25 years of experience in all aspects of employee benefits work. She is an attorney, and for the past 20 years, she has worked in public accounting, assisting clients with matters related to executive compensation and all manner of employee benefit plans. She has recent experience with respect to FATCA, assisting over 100 companies with FATCA compliance related to their non-US benefit plans. Christine also has experience with respect to the impact of the Affordable Care Act, the Common Reporting Standards (“CRS”), and Tax Reform on employers and the impact of Internal Revenue Code Sections 457A and 409A on global assignment policies, and related matters. 

She has assisted clients with the design and implementation of qualified benefit plans, cafeteria plans and health and various other welfare plans for multiple locations and business units, including qualified plan review and voluntary compliance. She has also designed and helped clients implement various types of executive incentive arrangements, including individual executive employment agreements, multiple types of equity plans, SERPs and severance pay programs. 

Christine has spoken at conferences across the country regarding employee benefits issues.  She is the author of “Cost & Benefit Factors – Ch. 6S” in IICLE’s publication, Employee Benefits Law.  She has extensive experience teaching in her areas of practice, conducting internal trainings and presenting at client and HR association round tables.  She is a frequent speaker at national and international forums (GEO, NASPP, TEI, Great Plains Federal Tax Institute, various bar associations, etc.).
Christine is a member of the Board of Directors and the Executive Board of Directors of the YWCA Metropolitan Chicago.
Christine has a J.D. from Vanderbilt University School of Law and a B.A. in English from Northwestern University.

headline: Leader. Innovator. Entrepreneur. Consultant.
topSkills: Leadership • Creativity and Innovation • P&L Management • Management Consulting • Business Transformation
about:
Brian currently serves as a US Commercial Office Leader at Deloitte Consulting.  His strategic focus harnesses Deloitte's global capabilities and the capabilities of the Firm’s Ecosystems/Alliances to foster novel collaborations with Clients that yield transformative, sustainable business value.

For nearly three decades, Brian has been a paragon of innovative and transformational leadership. His driving passion is to leverage the rich tapestry of his team's and his own diverse experiences to creatively address and solve the most complex business challenges faced by his Clients. This journey has seen him in a variety of roles over the years from Account and Offering Leader to steering multi-billion USD Management P&Ls.  In these capacities, Brian has consistently championed a high-performance, inclusive culture, strategically nurturing his team into tomorrow's influential leaders.

A notable innovation is his founding of The Smart Factory (TSF) by Deloitte @ Wichita (https://www.thesmartfactory.io), a pioneering, net-zero, immersive learning center that brings together an ecosystem of Alliances to shape the future of manufacturing and beyond. This initiative redefines how clients engage with and anticipate the impact of technological advancements on their future business landscape(s). Further extending his impact, Brian spearheaded the creation of Smart Factory Believers. This global, non-for-profit, purpose-driven program, powered by a Deloitte-led ecosystem, is dedicated to enhancing STEM education in underserved communities to support the cultivation of the workforce of the future.

Away from the Office, Brian resides in Chicago with his family. He is an avid traveler, sports enthusiast (with a noted Peloton passion), and a music aficionado, equally enjoying listening and playing music.

headline: Tax Partner at Deloitte
about:
I advise real estate investment fund managers on how to build and maintain tax efficient structures for raising capital and holding real estate assets.  This can get tricky when raising capital from public markets or various types of domestic, institutional, and foreign investors in the private sector.  Further complications arise as the geographic footprint expands and capital is invested in real estate assets across the nation and around the globe.  I help my clients navigate this complexity.  My focus is on supporting the CFOs and tax leaders of these organizations with identifying the opportunities and risks associated with evolving tax regulations, investor requirements, and market dynamics.

With over 25 years of experience, I specialize in advising real estate investment funds and REITs — public and private, investing equity and/or debt across all real estate asset classes — on structuring strategies and reporting that align with regulatory requirements and investor objectives.  My background includes deep knowledge of the tax considerations relevant to institutional and cross-border inbound investors, including the use of different vehicles — like REITs and corporate blockers — within tiered partnership structures to achieve optimal results.  I am also well versed on the qualifying criteria necessary to establish and preserve REIT status and the best practices used by REITs in both the public and private sector.

I am passionate about helping clients respond to changing market conditions — whether responding to distress or seizing new demand — by providing practical, strategic guidance that balances opportunity with risk management.  If you’re seeking a collaborative partner to help you navigate the intersection of real estate, tax, and investment strategy, let’s connect.

receivedRecommendations.description:
Greg's first position out of college was as a process engineer at an antiquated 3M Masking Tape Factory in the Chicago suburbs.  3M had decided to invest money in technical personnel in order to overcome decades of neglect to process equipment and process understanding.  Greg was given the assignment to improve both process understanding as well as to reduce waste.  Greg used modern methods, such as Design of Experiments, statistical analysis and first hand observation and experimentation to study the processes and make great improvements.  As a result Greg won a 3M Quality Improvement Award for using Design of Experiments to develop a new high performance Masking Tape for the Automotive Industry.  Greg developed instrumental methods, such as Xray Fluorescence, to unravel the secrets of the natural curative materials used to manufacture of Rubber-Resin Masking Tapes.
When I first hired Greg, I had all the confidence in the world that he would excel as a process engineer as well as any other thing he tackled, and I have been proven correct in that assessment.

headline: Managing Director at Deloitte
about:
MY CAREER
I’m an accomplished strategic senior leader, advisor and consultant recognized for successful design and execution of progressive and creative solutions to drive growth, development and operations by leveraging provider, hospital, health plan, academic, scientific and partnership assets.  My approach capitalizes on the knowledge and expertise of the team, identifying realistic stretch goals that establish a path for continued success, demonstrating the vision, engaging others, and executing with reasonable operational expectations.  I thrive on making an impactful difference for the people served, the team members, the organization, and the industry.  

MY LEADERSHIP STYLE
As a servant leader and innovator, I stretch others by seeking diverse opinions, cultivating trust, leading with authenticity and heart, empowering teams, and encouraging broad thinking. I believe meaningful purpose for the individual and business ultimately drives results.

MY STRENGTHS
Developing and executing strategy in challenging and ambiguous environments. Creating value via strategic partnerships and innovation. Empowering and guiding teams to create new solutions and solve complex business issues. Building cultures to foster collaboration and accountability.  Recruiting and developing top talent. 

TOP SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

Strategy Formulation and Execution | Planning | Business Development | Innovation | Affiliations | Partnerships | Mergers | Acquisitions | Provider Networks | Provider Relations | Marketing & Communications | System Integration | Board & Community Relations | Quality & Performance Improvement | Project Management | Centers of Excellence | Talent Development | Value Based Care | Population Health

experience.description: Stephanie has over 30 years of healthcare executive leadership, management and consulting experience focused in aligning strategy and operational execution across providers, health systems and payers.  She is a leader in Deloitte’s Value Based Care practice focused on enabling care model innovation with payment model reform.  Prior to joining Deloitte, she served as System Chief Strategy Officer for a vertically integrated delivery system which included multi-state health plans, tertiary and community hospitals, employed and affiliated provider networks, and a medical education/research partnership with a public university.   Stephanie is working to grow Deloitte’s healthcare innovation and transformation services within and across providers and payers.  She is currently focused in the areas of population health transformation; value-based care strategy; care delivery innovation aligned with payer contracting strategy; strategic payer partnerships; high performing provider networks; provider compensation/incentives; and care management design.

Contributed to design of AMC value proposition relative to payers and value based care contracting, development of data driven, fact based approach to guide the AMC in payer contract negotiations and establishment of data points and industry best practices to successfully negotiate favorable terms with the payer.

Led enterprise wide strategy, planning, business development, partnerships/M&A, growth, sales, and marketing/communications across hospitals, provider group, health insurance plans, and system subsidiaries. headline: Associate Director at Deloitte Consulting, UK | AI & Data | Technology and Transformation
about:
I am an Associate Director at Deloitte UK Consulting, aligned to Strategy, AI, Data and Analytics, with more than 13 years of experience.

I work closely with Public Sector clients helping deliver data and analytics solutions (including AI and Gen AI), starting from discovering key challenges, identifying metrics to quantify them with data available, figuring out initiatives to solve them through data and insights - to building platforms for integrating data from various sources and making it meaningful, accessible and available for end users to query, visualise and analyse, underpinned by good data governance and quality.

Before joining the UK firm in September’18, I was part of Deloitte Middle East, Dubai for more than 3 years, and was instrumental in building the Data & Analytics capability within the firm, focusing on data management (e.g. Integration, Warehouse, Governance & Quality) as well as data analytics (e.g. Reporting, Visualization, Centre of Excellence, Architecture & Roadmap).

Prior to that, I was with Deloitte India for almost 4 years, working on multiple end-to-end data driven Data Visualisation and Information Management implementation projects for CXOs including but not limited to requirement gathering, KPI discovery, data quality and integration, dashboard design and development, analytical reporting as well as training, user adoption and change management.

My primary area of interest is problem-solving using data and gaining valuable insights through intuitive analytics.

•Categorized services/clinics in the according to their utilization (high, medium and low) for actionable intelligence

projects.description:
Developed several designs for a Chevron Actuator. It was manufactured on a SOI wafer. The manufacturing process proceded as follows:
On a clean SOI wafer we deposited a chrome/gold conductive layer by using E-beam deposition. Our Photolithography stage was conducted with S1818 Photoresist. To create our structures we used S1818 photoresist for our masking process. We then etch the silicon device layer by using a reactive ion etching process.
